sections.heading: Metadata
sections.text:
Metadata helps search engines understand your content better (which can result in better SEO), and allows you to customize how your content is presented on social media, helping you create a more engaging and consistent user experience across various platforms.

The Metadata API in Next.js allows you to modify the `<head>` element of a page. You can configure metadata in two ways:

* **Config-based Metadata**: Export a [static `metadata` object](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-object) or a dynamic [`generateMetadata` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#generatemetadata-function) in a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.
* **File-based Metadata**: Add static or dynamically generated special files to route segments.

Additionally, you can create dynamic Open Graph Images using JSX and CSS with [imageResponse](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/image-response) constructor.

sections.heading: Analytics and Monitoring
sections.text:
For large applications, Next.js integrates with popular analytics and monitoring tools to help you understand how your application is performing. Learn more in the  [OpenTelemetry](/docs/pages/building-your-application/optimizing/open-telemetry) and [Instrumentation](/docs/pages/building-your-application/optimizing/instrumentation) guides.

- [Images](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/images)
  - Optimize your images with the built-in `next/image` component.
- [Fonts](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/fonts)
  - Optimize your application's web fonts with the built-in `next/font` loaders.
- [Scripts](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/scripts)
  - Optimize 3rd party scripts with the built-in Script component.
- [Metadata](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/metadata)
  - Use the Metadata API to define metadata in any layout or page.
- [Static Assets](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/static-assets)
  - Next.js allows you to serve static files, like images, in the public directory. You can learn how it works here.
- [Bundle Analyzer](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/bundle-analyzer)
  - Analyze the size of your JavaScript bundles using the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin.
- [Lazy Loading](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/lazy-loading)
  - Lazy load imported libraries and React Components to improve your application's loading performance.
- [Analytics](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/analytics)
  - Measure and track page performance using Next.js Speed Insights
- [Instrumentation](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/instrumentation)
  - Learn how to use instrumentation to run code at server startup in your Next.js app
- [OpenTelemetry](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/open-telemetry)
  - Learn how to instrument your Next.js app with OpenTelemetry.
- [Third Party Libraries](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/third-party-libraries)
  - Optimize the performance of third-party libraries in your application with the `@next/third-parties` package.

---

skills.name: Image Component Optimization
skills.description: Optimize image delivery by implementing lazy loading and automatic device-based resizing. Use when rendering images in responsive web layouts to reduce initial page load time and improve performance.
skills.skill_body: Apply the Image Component to abstract image optimization complexity. The component lazy-loads images on viewport entry and automatically resizes based on device screen size. Ensure images are wrapped with the Image Component rather than native tags to enable these optimizations. ## Objective optimize_image_delivery ## Applicable Signals - rendering images in responsive web layouts - need to reduce initial page load time - multiple images on a single page - images of varying sizes across device breakpoints ## Contraindications - static images with fixed dimensions that do not require responsiveness - images already served from CDN with built-in optimization - critical above-the-fold images where lazy loading would delay visibility ## Intervention Moves - Replace native elements with Image Component - Configure device-based sizing rules - Verify lazy-load behavior on viewport entry ## Workflow Steps - Identify images in the layout that would benefit from lazy loading and responsive resizing - Replace native tags with Image Component - Configure device-based sizing parameters - Test lazy-load behavior and responsive resizing across target devices ## Constraints - Image Component must be used instead of native tags to enable optimization - Device size detection must be available in the rendering environment ## Cautions - Lazy loading may delay image visibility; consider eager loading for critical above-the-fold images - Automatic resizing requires device size context; verify breakpoint configuration matches design requirements ## Output Contract - Images load lazily on viewport entry - Image dimensions adapt to device screen size without layout shift - Page load time is reduced compared to native implementation

skills.name: Link Prefetching Strategy
skills.description: Prefetch linked pages in the background to enable faster and smoother page transitions. Use when implementing internal page links to reduce perceived latency during navigation.
skills.skill_body:
When a user hovers over or focuses on an internal link, prefetch the target page's resources in the background. This allows the page transition to complete without visible loading delay when the user clicks. Do not prefetch external links or heavy resources in bandwidth-constrained environments.

## Objective

accelerate_navigation
## Applicable Signals

- Internal link element detected
- Page transition latency is a performance concern
- User interaction with link is imminent

## Contraindications

- External links to third-party domains
- Links to heavy resources that should not be preloaded
- Bandwidth-constrained or metered network environments
- User has disabled prefetching preferences

## Intervention Moves

- Configure Link component to prefetch target page resources
- Trigger prefetch on user hover or focus event

## Workflow Steps

- Identify internal navigation links in the application
- Configure Link component to prefetch target page resources
- Trigger prefetch on user hover or focus event
- Complete page transition on user click without additional loading

## Constraints

- Only prefetch internal links within the application
- Respect user network conditions and data-saver preferences
- Do not prefetch resources that are not necessary for immediate page load

## Cautions

- Excessive prefetching may consume unnecessary bandwidth
- Monitor prefetch success rate to avoid wasted resources

## Output Contract

- Target page resources are prefetched before user click; page transition completes without visible loading delay.

skills.name: Third-Party Script Loading Control
skills.description: Manage loading and execution timing of third-party scripts to prevent performance degradation and blocking of the main thread. Use when integrating analytics, ads, or external services that do not block initial page render.
skills.skill_body:
Use the Script Component to wrap third-party scripts. Configure the loading strategy (e.g., afterInteractive, lazyOnload, or worker) based on script priority and dependency. Verify that scripts load asynchronously and do not block the main rendering thread.

## Objective

control_script_execution
## Applicable Signals

- External script dependency identified
- Analytics or tracking service integration required
- Third-party ad network or service integration
- Performance audit reveals script blocking

## Contraindications

- Critical inline scripts required for initial page render
- Scripts with no external dependencies or performance impact
- Synchronous scripts that must execute before page interaction

## Intervention Moves

- Wrap third-party script in Script Component
- Select appropriate loading strategy (afterInteractive, lazyOnload, worker, or beforeInteractive)
- Verify script executes asynchronously without blocking main thread
- Test page interactivity during and after script load

## Workflow Steps

- {'step': 3, 'action': 'Select loading strategy: afterInteractive (default), lazyOnload, worker, or beforeInteractive'}

- {'step': 6, 'action': 'Test page interactivity and performance metrics'}

## Constraints

- Script Component must be used for third-party scripts only
- Loading strategy must match script priority and dependency chain
- Main thread blocking must be prevented

## Cautions

- Verify script dependencies are resolved before execution
- Test script execution order if multiple third-party scripts are present
- Monitor for race conditions between script loads

## Output Contract

- Third-party scripts load asynchronously without blocking the main thread; execution timing is controlled per script strategy; page remains interactive during script load.
